review_scope: Authenticated FastAPI reads and commands; immutable artifact import, paging, cursors and ownership; the fixed zero-budget local_git_inspection pipeline; and host subprocess boundaries. No candidate source was edited.

commands.result: 21 tests passed, 0 failed. Includes HTTPX auth/paging/traversal/binary-content checks and the actual B/D modules on a disposable temporary Git fixture.
Help shows the loopback entrypoint and data/config/runtime, token, allowed-root, worker, adapter argv, port and timeout settings. services/runtime/README.md documents startup and secret placement.

commands.command: Focused HTTPX auth/CORS/token probe with RuntimeApiTests temporary fixture
commands.result: Unauthenticated /v1/capabilities returned 403; /health returned 200; authenticated capabilities returned 200; no Access-Control-* response header and no token in either response.

commands.command: Disposable HTTPX long-line and manifest-page bound probe
commands.result: A 150,000-byte line of quote characters returned a 300,264-byte text response. A 150,000-byte diff row returned a 300,837-byte diff response. A 100-entry manifest page with long valid relative paths returned 303,614 bytes. Each exceeds the documented 262,144-byte page limit.

With a 1-second adapter timeout, a fake B wrote a valid response, spawned a 20-second child inheriting stdout/stderr, and exited. AdapterRunner reported B adapter timed out, but the child PID remained alive; the probe killed it.

findings.title: Timeout and cancellation can leave adapter descendants running
findings.detail: _terminate returns as soon as the direct process has a returncode. asyncio process.wait can remain pending while a descendant holds inherited stdout/stderr open, so the timeout path reaches _terminate after the adapter has exited and skips killing its process group. The reproduced child remained alive after the request was reported timed out. Such a child can continue using the assigned workspace or output root after A marks the attempt failed or cancelled.

findings.title: Serialized artifact pages exceed the 256 KiB limit
findings.detail: Text and diff paging budgets count UTF-8 source bytes before JSON escaping and omit response-field overhead. A 150,000-byte line of quote characters therefore expands to a 300,264-byte text response; the equivalent diff row produced 300,837 bytes. The manifest-files route limits entry count but does not bound serialized bytes; the 100-entry probe produced 303,614 bytes. This exceeds COMPUTER_UI.md's 256 KiB page ceiling.

verified: All /v1 routes exercised require the bearer token; /health is the public endpoint. The app installs no CORS middleware, token comparison uses hmac.compare_digest, and the tested token was not returned in responses.

The supported run gate is derived from stored source/check/action/budget/task data; the API rejects a coding-profile job.run, and the scheduler revalidates the persisted inspection profile. Coding capability and worker model verification remain false.

The fixed pipeline invokes only B repo.inspect, B repo.prepare, B artifacts.freeze, and D check.run. Its candidate manifest and snapshot are rehashed before D checks the staged manifest and read-only frozen tree. No model/provider call or delivery operation is enabled by AdapterRunner's allowlist.

Artifact reads use registered IDs and digest-checked content; path traversal and binary text access are rejected. HMAC cursors reject malformed/noncanonical values and are scoped to the requested job/artifact data in exercised cases.

Inspection jobs use a zero-dollar reservation; completed run usage token counts remain null and known cost remains zero. The HTTP and real B/D fixture runs reached verifying with no product job, provider call, or external delivery.
limits_vs_full_A2: This candidate implements only the fixed single-task local_git_inspection profile. The A2-2 general scheduler acceptance for disjoint-task overlap, dependency ordering and overlapping write-scope serialization is not implemented or tested; coding/model execution remains unavailable as instructed for this MVP profile.

A hard-killed runtime has no A3 reconciliation path in this candidate. Startup does not reconcile persisted running attempts; the affected job can remain running and cannot be explicitly rerun. No automatic duplicate dispatch was observed or enabled, but restart recovery remains an A3 requirement.

A2-3 interaction/idle model-call counting is not a runtime UI test here. The runtime route and adapter allowlist inspection shows reads do not dispatch work, and the fixed check reports zero inference calls.
fixture_live_distinction: All API and subprocess probes used disposable temporary databases, paths and Git fixtures. No registered user repository, primary source file, product job, provider/model service, external delivery, or spending was used.
